title: Saudi Arabia
attribution: World Climate Simulation materials by Climate Interactive, MIT Sloan, and the UMass Lowell Climate Change Initiative. Updated November 2025. Adapted for nested-agent experiments.
goals: Protect oil export revenues and the role of hydrocarbons in the global economy
Advance the Saudi Green Initiative's afforestation goals and a 2060 net-zero target
negotiating_constraints: Resist language that phases out fossil fuels; favour emissions-focused approaches such as carbon capture
Developed nations bear historic responsibility, so there is no obligation to contribute climate finance
The economic impact of climate policy on fossil fuel exporters must be addressed
opportunities: Very large solar and wind potential
Carbon capture and the circular carbon economy
adaptation_notes: No World Climate briefing exists for Saudi Arabia. Its members read the Other Developing Nations briefing, which covers most of the Middle East. The goals, constraints, opportunities and risks below are author-written summaries of public positions up to November 2025. Goals and qualitative constraints paraphrase the briefing. Baseline commitments, numeric ceilings, finance-role restrictions, personalities and scoring are author-created experimental assumptions, NOT official prescribed positions. Source text reflects November 2025 and is not a live policy fact-check.
